title: Knowledge check: Vue Rendering Architectures

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Vue Rendering Architectures”?
options: SSR output should hydrate deterministically and mutable state must not be unintentionally shared across requests.
window is available while rendering on every server.
SSG output changes automatically on every API update without rebuilding.
A local development server proves production hosting routes work.
questions.answer_key: SSR output should hydrate deterministically and mutable state must not be unintentionally shared across requests.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Vue Rendering Architectures directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Client-side rendering (CSR)”, which practice is most reliable?
options: window is available while rendering on every server.
SSG output changes automatically on every API update without rebuilding.
A local development server proves production hosting routes work.
SSR output should hydrate deterministically and mutable state must not be unintentionally shared across requests.
questions.answer_key: SSR output should hydrate deterministically and mutable state must not be unintentionally shared across requests.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Client-side rendering (CSR)”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Vue Rendering Architectures” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.

review_note: Answer keys and explanations are server-side data. Human review required before publication.
